warning_texts: Both test claims store p as 0.0000000000 while their display_digits is 4. At either precision the page would show p as exactly zero. The true p values are far below any displayable bound (z = 26.72, t = 42.70) but they are not zero, so the release should say 'below 0.0001' rather than print a zero.

The n field of each estimate claim is an integer while metrics carries n as a string. The values are equal (24597, 19934, 17818, 12055) but not byte-equal, which matters if a later rule compares them as text.

The CLM-COMPLETION-* claims compute their denominators correctly over the whole channel, cancelled and pending included: 24597 direct and 19934 partner orders, recounted. No caveat says this in words, and a reader of the release cannot tell the rate was not filtered to completed orders.

All four estimate claims use the caveat wording 'one quarter of orders in this channel'. A reader can take 'one quarter' as a fraction of 25% rather than the calendar quarter; 'orders placed in 2026-Q1 in this channel' says the same without the ambiguity.

R04 carries no caveats. The sampling-interval caveat for the AOV intervals exists only in the claim register, so an answer file rendered on its own would show intervals with no statement of what they mean.

The machine gate's gaps line up with the blockers above. No rule reads the wording of analysis/answers/*.json, and caveats_declared requires neither delivered-only nor net-of-refunds for the AOV claims. On both points this audit's judgment is the only check.

claims_are_single_assertions reports 'all roles in p' for both test claims, yet their render_values give the statistic and effect in units statistic, proportion_difference and cohens_d. The rule's description of these claims is not accurate, even though the claims are fine as single assertions.

The effect size of H-CHANNEL-AOV is Cohen's d with the pooled standard deviation: my recount gives 0.4868998682, matching the claim. The averaged-variance variant gives 0.4950. Neither the claim nor the plan names which variant is meant, so the release should label it.
summary: Every number in the eight claims matches an independent recalculation from quarantine/orders.csv (one row per order after keeping the last revision, 2026-01..2026-03, negative refunds excluded): 44531 orders, 3023296.61 EUR net revenue, both Wilson and both Student intervals, and both registered tests. Each claim also agrees field by field with metrics and analysis_plan.json. Country and month strata show no Simpson reversal. The text around the numbers fails in four places.
